records.claim: Legacy CM1950: the sample space cannot be evacuated. The IFU's only 'vacuum' is the optional section-waste vacuum extractor (suction nozzle with adjustable intensity); the cryochamber is an atmospheric cabinet closed by a heated sliding window that the operator opens to work, and the complete Technical Data give no chamber pressure/vacuum specification. module.vacuum_system (section-waste extraction) must not be read as vacuum.available.
records.value_as_printed: VAC = vacuum extractor for section waste (no evacuable chamber)
records.document_title: Leica CM1950 Cryostat, Instructions for Use, English, Order No. 14 0477 8U101 - Revision ZA, Version 3.0, Revision ZA - 05.2024
records.location: Chapter 7 Instrument Controls, printed page 43 (VAC button); Chapter 5 General Overview, printed page 28, Fig. 8 item 1 (heated sliding window); Chapter 3 Technical Data
records.quote: Press the VAC button to enable the vacuum extractor. The LED in the VAC button is lit while the extractor is on. Press the button again to disable it. • Use the knob to adjust the intensity of the vacuum.
records.reasoning: An open-front cryostat cabinet accessed through a sliding window is physically not an evacuable sample space; the full manual defines the vacuum function as suction of section waste.

records.claim: DualEcoTec CM1950 STANDARD: the sample space cannot be evacuated. The product page describes a spacious cryocabinet in which the operator organizes tools, blades, freezing media and glass slides (an atmospheric working cabinet); the only vacuum item in any configuration is the 'Vacuum extraction system' (section waste), which STANDARD does not include.
records.value_as_printed: spacious cryocabinet; vacuum extraction system only in VACUUM and VACUUM/MOTOR configurations
records.document_title: Leica CM1950 | Clinical Cryostat (Leica CM1950 - The Cryostat with DualEcoTec cooling system)
records.location: Overview section; Configurations section
records.quote: For an efficient workflow, all instruments come with a spacious cryocabinet to facilitate handling of multiple specimens. The cryostat provides sufficient space to organize your tools, blades, freezing media, and glass slides.
records.reasoning: A cabinet holding tools, slides and freezing media during operation is at atmospheric pressure; with the complete configuration list showing no evacuable chamber, evacuation is outside the instrument category.

not_found.searched: Full text of IFU V3.0 Rev ZA (Leica-hosted PDF), legacy manual V1.1 (ASU-hosted) and older IFU (UCR-hosted), US/global DualEcoTec product pages, flyers 250760 Rev A and 250384 Rev A; Lune and Consensus paper search. No dry-gas purge of the cryochamber is mentioned; not recorded as absence because a gas purge is not physically outside the instrument category and no source states its absence.

US/global DualEcoTec product pages and flyers 250760/250384: no window, viewport or illumination is described for Gen B (Gen B IFU not reachable: files.leicabiosystems.com/US/en?keycode=CM1950 returns 404; brochure 211322 Rev A is gated). The Gen A value (heated sliding window) was not extended across generations.

US/global product pages, flyers 250760/250384, shop.leicabiosystems.com pid-14047740046 (55 mm disc page names no instrument generation). The Gen B page mentions only 'specimen discs with deep groove design' without diameters.

IFU V3.0 Rev ZA Technical Data p.23, brochure 95.7826 Rev F p.7, legacy manual V1.1 (ASU) and older IFU (UCR): all give only 'Maximum specimen size 50 x 80 mm' (two dimensions). Optional accessories list an 80 x 50 mm specimen disc but no maximum specimen thickness/depth. See corrections for the axis assignment of the 50 mm figure.
Any-of requirement: vacuum.available is recorded as an absence (see records); purge.gas was not found (see above), so only the vacuum branch of the any-of pair is resolved.
